newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates mixed, govt paper yields easier.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates mixed, govt paper yields easier.

text.p: Hong Kong interbank rates were mixed in quiet trading on Tuesday while government paper yields were slightly eaiser as U.S. long bond yields continued to stay at low levels, dealers said.
One-week bills yielded 4.61 percent, down from 4.73 at Monday midday, three-year note yields eased to 5.90 from 5.91 percent and the seven-year yielded 6.77 versus 6.79 percent.
The longest 10-year notes yielded 7.02 versus 7.03 percent.
"Trading of government paper was pretty quiet this morning with participants waiting for the tender results of the 28-date Exchange Fund bills," a Japanese bank dealer said.

Dealers said the tender results, released shortly before noon, was reasonable since the average accepted yield of 4.54 percent was fairly close to the secondary market. One-month bills yielded 4.59 percent on Tuesday versus 4.62 on Monday.

"The market is relatively calm this time and the demand for short-date bills is not so keen after the Hong Kong Monetary Authority said it would tender one more 28-day issue at an expanded size of HK$10 billion on Thursaday," a dealer said.
In the pervious tender last week there was an approximately 20 basis point difference between tender yields and bill yields in the secondary market.
Banks are accumulating short-dated Exchange Fund bills in preparation for the implementation of the Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system in December 9.

In the interbank market, overnight cash eased to 5-1/4 3/16 percent from 5-7/16 3/8 with light offers seen in short-dated money of one-month and below, dealers said. Three-month money was up slightly to 5-5/8 1/2 percent against 5-1/2 9/16 percent.
"Short-term money under the year end effect will continue to be a bit tight this month while longer-term cash could ease slightly in view of low U.S. long bond yields," one dealer said.
